claims.text: Under the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\), let \(p=c=1\), \(a=1\), \(b=3\). Then \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(\min(i,j)=3\), and \(d=ij\). Put \[ P_{x,y}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},y)}\quad(y=0\text{ omitted}). \] The complete Schur-column sets in degrees \(d+k\), \(0\le k\le3\), are \(\{P_{x,y}:x+y=k\}\).

Writing \[ X_k=P_{k,0},\quad Y_k=P_{0,k},\quad Z=P_{1,1},\quad A=P_{2,1},\quad B=P_{1,2}, \] the complete Pieri-row lattices are \[ \mathcal R_d=0,\qquad \mathcal R_{d+1}=\mathbb Z(X_1+Y_1), \] \[ \mathcal R_{d+2}= \mathbb Z(Z+Y_2)+\mathbb Z(X_2+Z), \] and \[ \mathcal R_{d+3}= \mathbb Z(X_3+A)+\mathbb Z(A+B)+\mathbb Z(B+Y_3). \]

Retaining the horizontal proposed family \[ F_X=(X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3), \] complementary minors in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2,d+3\) have determinants \(1,1,1,1\), respectively. In degrees \(d+2,d+3\), use rows \((X_2+Z,Z+Y_2)\) and \((X_3+A,A+B,B+Y_3)\), giving \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}_{(Z,Y_2)},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}_{(A,B,Y_3)}. \]

Retaining the vertical proposed family \[ F_Y=(X_0,Y_1,Y_2,Y_3), \] also gives complementary minors of determinant \(1\). In degrees \(d+2,d+3\), on complementary columns \((X_2,Z)\) and \((X_3,A,B)\), the same selected rows yield \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}. \]

Consequently, in the truncated quotient through degree \(d+3\), \[ \bar Y_1=-\bar X_1,\qquad \bar Y_2=\bar X_2,\qquad \bar Y_3=-\bar X_3, \] and each of \(F_X,F_Y\) is a degreewise integral basis of the truncated quotient.

The requested target—complete Pieri row lattices in degrees \(d,\ldots,d+3\) and explicit unimodular complementary minors retaining the four proposed generators—is established, conditional on the stated integral presentation hypotheses.
